page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 2.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a 1.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, AES cryptography, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the n2-highcpu-2 demonstrates entry-level performance characteristics. Stress-ng single-core CPU performance is measured at 1399.29, while multi-core performance reaches 1841.88. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 1111.0 and a multi-core score of 1311.0, with software compilation using Clang scoring 1719.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 102.26 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 13.72 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 11.78 GB/sec for large-block writes. Cryptographic performance is reflected in a PassMark CPU encryption score of 839.13.

Given its low memory-to-CPU ratio and modest performance scores, the n2-highcpu-2 is positioned as a cost-efficient option for lightweight, compute-focused tasks that do not demand large memory footprints. It achieves 1.75 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 2.06 GB/sec. For machine learning, it can process small 135M parameter LLM prompts at 116.03 tokens per second and generate text at 34.34 tokens per second. This instance is best suited for basic web serving, lightweight background processing, simple text processing, and small-scale utility workloads.
